samples.summary: The `findBlock` hardening of `getSelectedImage` / `updateSelectedImage` is claimed but never exercised: only `selectImageAt` is tested against a missing block
samples.evidence: The new test at copy-integrity.test.ts:1176-1188 is headed "selecting an image in a block that is gone returns rather than throws" and its comment asserts "`selectImageAt` / `getSelectedImage` / `updateSelectedImage` all read the selection coordinate through `findBlock`". But the body only calls `expect(() => editor.selectImageAt('gone', 0)).not.toThrow()`. The follow-up `expect(editor.getSelectedImage()).toBeNull()` is vacuous for the hardening under test: `selectImageAt('gone', 0)` returns before setting `selectedImage`, so `selectedImage` is still null and `getSelectedImage` returns null at its `if (!selectedImage) return null` guard (editor.ts:3809) without ever reaching the changed `doc.findBlock(selectedImage.blockId)` at editor.ts:3812. The scenario the diff hardens against — a LIVE `selectedImage` whose block has since disappeared (remote edit / uncleared mutation) — is never constructed, so reverting editor.ts:3812 and 3826 back to `getBlock` (which throws) would leave the whole suite green. `updateSelectedImage`'s `findBlock` (editor.ts:3826) has no test at all. Searched the whole `packages/docs/test` tree for `getSelectedImage|updateSelectedImage`; every other use has the block present.

samples.summary: `mergeTableCells` gains a `clearImageSelectionForMutation()` call but is the one table-structure op omitted from the new parameterised table-op test list

samples.evidence: The diff adds `imageResizeDrag = null;` alongside `selectedImage = null;` in `resetAfterDocumentReplace` (editor.ts:3913-3914). The new test at copy-integrity.test.ts:1163-1174 only asserts `getSelectedImage()` is null; it never starts a resize drag, and there is no API surface asserted on drag state. `packages/docs/test/view/image-selection-overlay.test.ts` only tests the pure helpers (`handleCenter`, `hitTestImageHandle`, `computePreviewRect`), never the editor's `imageResizeDrag` field. verdict.reason: The `findBlock` hardening in the public `getSelectedImage` (editor.ts:3812) and `updateSelectedImage` (editor.ts:3826) is not exercised by any test. The new test (copy-integrity.test.ts:1177-1188) only calls `selectImageAt('gone', 0)`, which bails at editor.ts:3799-3800 without setting `selectedImage`; the follow-up `expect(editor.getSelectedImage()).toBeNull()` therefore returns at the `if (!selectedImage) return null` guard (editor.ts:3807) and never reaches line 3812. Every other `getSelectedImage()` assertion in the suite either runs with the block present, or runs after a path that already nulled `selectedImage` (deleteSelectedImageInline editor.ts:2313-2318 for tests at 627-676; resetAfterDocumentReplace editor.ts:3907-3913 for test 1163). The genuine stale-selection tests (copy-integrity.test.ts:558-586, 588-609) assert through the clipboard event, which reads the separate `imageSelectionProvider` site (editor.ts:2330-2341), not the API method. Repo-wide grep for `updateSelectedImage`/`getSelectedImage`/`selectImageAt`/`SelectedImage` across all file types shows `updateSelectedImage` has zero callers in any test (only editor.ts:328/3822/3988), so its guard has no coverage at all. Since `Doc.getBlock` throws on a missing id (document.ts:174-186), reverting 3812/3826 to `getBlock` would leave the whole suite green — the definition of a missing test over a changed guard. No counterexample found anywhere in packages/docs, packages/frontend, or elsewhere.
